name: Pedaiah
overview: Pedaiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Jehoiachin (also known as Jeconiah). His lineage places him within the Davidic line, which is significant in the biblical genealogies. Beyond this, there are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Pedaiah means "YHWH ransoms," reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with the covenantal relationship between God and His people. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:18 and was not specifically given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Pedaiah as the son of Jehoiachin. It is also inferred that Pedaiah was the father of Zerubbabel and Shimei, linking him to important figures in the post-exilic period. These relationships situate him firmly within the royal lineage of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Pedaiah’s significance lies in his place within the royal genealogy of Judah, particularly as the son of Jehoiachin and the father of Zerubbabel, who played a pivotal role in the restoration of Jerusalem after the exile. His mention in 1 Chronicles 3 highlights the continuity of God’s covenant promises through the Davidic line, which ultimately points forward to the coming of the Messiah. Though not prominent in narrative events, his genealogical role underscores God’s faithfulness in preserving His chosen lineage.
